x: On the other hand our runners continue to improve, for in the 2 miles Invitation team race Newell (9-18.4), Dabbs (9-23.8) and Robinson (9-30.2) were only 5 points behind the winners, Polytechnic.

Commenting on the previous autumn's Southern race "Olympian" had written"---a moderate performance with a few bright spots in the form of Bhatia, Black and Dabbs." Ranjit had raced in third on the first leg.
Kerr, Newell, Davies, Walker, Black, Dabbs, Linstead, Maclean. How's that for a line up to set a new 3 mile record?
Sandwiched between Black and Forey the four runners on "trial" were Davies, Dabbs, Thresher, and Miller. The two Johns won the day, but there was little else of interest to Belgrave.

Our turnout for this fixture against Mitcham A.C. and Croydon H. was most disappointing for, besides having a team performing in the Hogs Back race, we were also without the services of Kerr, Dabbs, and Linstead who were unfortunately unavailable.
Injuries to Kerr, Dabbs and Davies and the absence of our usual spear-head,Pat Newell, did not augur well for our chances before we had even left London.
Much of the glamour was robbed from the event due to the unavoidable absence of the North brothers, Thresher & Dabbs who were competing at major meetings.

The only event for Seniors alone was the 2 miles where Bill Kerr lead from gun to tape in 9:10.2, ahead of Dabbs and Fairclough. Chris Ryan scored a junior sprint double over Turnverein's Rotharmel (10.3 and 23.5) but only managed it by a whisker in the 220 yards.

Yet during our recent lean years, the name of Pat Newell has figured consistently and he has, along with other stalwarts like Walker, Linstead, Dabbs, Davies and Maclean, Helped keep the Belgrave flag flying, albeit a little limply.
Unfortunately the fixture clashed with Inter-Counties Championships and an international race on the continent,which meant we were without the North brothers,Thresher,Dabbs and Fairclough.

Tony Fairclough,although still below peak,was third until the last mile when he was overhauled by a fast finishing trio,but was well pleased with the result - as indeed was Dabbs who was surprised to make the team so easily.
Seniors:North 3rd,North 15th,Hart 23rd,Fairclough 24th,Dabbs 29th,O'Hara 51st. Juniors:Bicourt 23rd,Cocks 51st,Hampshire 53rd,Morrison 119th---Belgrave 7th.
Could we do it this season with the following scorers ? SURREY: Gerry North, Thresher, Fairclough, Steer, Dabbs, Black. MIDDLESEX: Hart, O'Hara, Kerr, Newell, Dear and Crookes.
North, O'Hara, Dabbs, Thorpe and Black were to be joined by Hugh Barrow for the "National" at Sheffield, leaving runners of the class of Steer, Reilly and Hart as reserves.

In the "longs" a buoyant mood is apparent with STEER, DABBS, MANN And HART Corp. moving steadily forward. The index, rallying towards the close was depressed on the news that HERCULES was making a bid for SATCHELL.

I wonder what Thresher, Fairclough, Major, Bicourt, O'Hara, Hart, Dabbs, Steer etc. think of that. Agreed that the North brothers, Dance, Whewell, Williams, Kerr and others have played parts of varying degrees in our success but they joined us on moving to London because they had to change their club.

… Robinson, Miller, Shippen and Thompson; out on the dimly lit roads of Wimbledon on Thursdays, gasping behind Linstead, Dabbs, Gebbett & Co. as they did the "seven hills"; sometimes on the "Warren 9" with Bird, Walker, Baulch & Co.…
